summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with bright red blood per rectum and worsening back pain. Evaluation revealed L5-S1 osteomyelitis and discitis, confirmed by CT and MRI, leading to a two-stage spinal fusion. He underwent anterior partial vertebrectomy and fusion on 2175-09-07, followed by posterior laminectomy and instrumentation on 2175-09-10. The source of GI bleeding was likely hemorrhoidal, with no recurrence. He developed acute kidney injury post-contrast, managed supportively, and recovered. He received blood products intraoperatively and WinRho after Rh-mismatched platelet transfusion. Osteoporosis was diagnosed intraoperatively; tamoxifen was stopped, and calcium/vitamin D started. He completed antibiotic transition planning, with vancomycin to continue via PICC for six weeks. He was discharged to extended care with stable mental status, ambulating with assistance, and pain controlled on oral medications.
